text: Samson went to Gaza, where he saw a prostitute and went in to spend the night with her.

The people of Gaza were told, Samson has come here. So they surrounded the place and waited for him all night at the city gate, staying quiet through the night, saying, Let's wait until dawn, then we'll kill him.

But Samson lay there only until midnight; then he got up, took hold of the doors of the city gate along with the two posts, pulled them out with the bar and all, put them on his shoulders, and carried them to the top of the hill facing Hebron.
After this, he fell in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek named Delilah.

The Philistine rulers went to her and said, Seduce him and find out where his great strength comes from, and how we can overpower him, bind him, and subdue him; each of us will give you eleven hundred pieces of silver.
So Delilah said to Samson, Please tell me the secret of your great strength, and how you could be tied up and made helpless.
Samson told her, If they tie me with seven fresh bowstrings that haven't been dried, I will become weak, like anyone else.
The Philistine rulers brought her seven fresh bowstrings, and she tied him with them.

With men lying in ambush in an inner room, she cried, The Philistines are upon you, Samson! But he snapped the bowstrings the way a strand of yarn snaps when it touches fire, and the secret of his strength remained unknown.
Then Delilah said to Samson, You have made a fool of me and lied to me; please tell me how you can be tied.
He said, If they tie me tightly with new ropes that have never been used, I will become weak, like anyone else.
So Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them, then cried, The Philistines are upon you, Samson! With men waiting in ambush in the room, he snapped the ropes off his arms like threads.

Delilah said to Samson, Up to now you have made a fool of me and lied to me; tell me how you can be tied. He answered, If you weave the seven braids of my hair into the fabric on your loom and secure it with a pin, I will become weak, like anyone else.

So while he slept, Delilah wove the seven braids of his hair into the loom's fabric and fastened it with the pin. Again she cried, The Philistines are upon you, Samson! He woke from his sleep and pulled out the pin, the loom, and the fabric.
Then she said to him, How can you say you love me when you won't confide in me? This is the third time you've made a fool of me and haven't told me where your great strength comes from.
She pestered him with her words day after day and pressed him until he was tired to death.

So he told her everything. No razor has ever been used on my head, he said, because I have been a Nazirite to God since before I was born. If my head were shaved, my strength would leave me, and I would become weak, like anyone else.

When Delilah realized he had told her everything, she sent word to the Philistine rulers, saying, Come once more, for he has told me everything. So the rulers came to her, bringing the silver with them.
She lulled him to sleep on her lap, called for a man, and had him shave off the seven braids of his hair; she began to subdue him, and his strength left him.
Then she called out, The Philistines are upon you, Samson! He woke from his sleep and thought, I'll go out as before and shake myself free — but he didn't know that the LORD had left him.
The Philistines seized him, gouged out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza, where they bound him with bronze shackles, and he was made to grind grain in the prison.
But the hair on his head began to grow back after it had been shaved.
Now the Philistine rulers gathered to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon and to celebrate, saying, Our god has handed Samson our enemy over to us.
When the people saw him, they praised their god, saying, Our god has handed our enemy over to us, the one who destroyed our land and killed so many of us.
Once their spirits were high, they said, Bring out Samson to entertain us. So they called Samson out of the prison, and he performed for them; they stood him between the pillars.
Samson said to the boy who held his hand, Let me feel the pillars supporting the building, so I can lean against them.
Now the building was crowded with men and women; all the Philistine rulers were there, and about three thousand men and women were on the roof watching Samson entertain them.
Then Samson cried out to the LORD, Lord GOD, please remember me. Please strengthen me just once more, God, so that I may pay back the Philistines at once for my two eyes.
Samson took hold of the two central pillars supporting the building and pushed against them, one hand on each,

and said, Let me die with the Philistines! He pushed with all his strength, and the building collapsed on the rulers and everyone inside it. So those he killed at his death were more than those he had killed during his life.
His brothers and his father's whole family came down, took his body, carried it back, and buried it between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of his father Manoah. He had judged Israel for twenty years.
